entries.text: Thank you for calling VeloFit. Your call may be recorded for quality assurance. Please hold for the next available agent.
Thank you for holding. My name is Alex. How can I help you today?
Yeah, I need to return these absolutely worthless cycling shoes I bought. This is a complete joke.
I can certainly look into that for you. I'm sorry to hear you're not happy with your purchase. Do you have your order number handy?
It's VF88602. And let me be clear, I want a full refund, not some store credit nonsense. I'm not spending another dime here.

Okay, one moment. I'm pulling up order VF88602. I see the VeloFit cycling shoes, delivered 43 days ago. To make sure I understand correctly, what specifically is the issue with them? Is it a technical fault or a preference issue?
The issue is they're torture devices! I went on one ride and they gave me horrible blisters on both heels. I've tried adjusting the cleats, everything. They're garbage and I want my money back.
I understand your frustration, and getting blisters is definitely not the experience we want for our customers. I'm just checking our return policy for you now.
There's nothing to check! Either you give me my refund or I'm speaking to a manager and telling everyone I know how terrible your products are. I'm not playing games.
That won't be necessary, sir. I can resolve this for you. According to our policy, you're well within the 90-day return window. I can go ahead and process this return for a full refund right now.
Fine. About time. So what happens now?

I'm generating a prepaid return label that I'll email to you in the next few minutes. Just pack the shoes back in their box, attach the label, and drop them off. Once our warehouse receives them, the refund will be processed back to your original payment method.
Make sure that email comes through. I'm watching for it.
I've just sent it. It should be in your inbox shortly. Is there anything else I can help you with today?
No. Just make sure I get my money.
